messages:
mike-csm: FYI: ACME escalated — their external action 'order_submit' started receiving the wrong payload after yesterday's request-router rollout.
mike-csm: Customer says orders were created with empty items arrays and order_id pushed into customer_notes instead of body.order_id. They're blocked in prod.
mike-csm: sample request id: r-239847, attached logs below.

sara-support: Can you paste the raw payload + response for that request id? Any client-side changes? @alex-ml @jordan-se

mike-csm: here's the log snippet:
```
REQ r-239847 -> route: /v1/chat -> variant: router-v2
payload: {"action":"order_submit","body":{"order_id":"A123","items":[{"sku":"x","qty":1}]},"meta":{}}
RESP r-239847 <- downstream: action-invoke 200
invoke_payload_received_by-customer_backend: {"order_id":"A123","items":[],"customer_notes":"A123"}
```

sara-support: oof. That looks like the items array got flattened/truncated and order_id copied into notes. No client changes reported?

mike-csm: customer confirms no client changes. Issue started right after router-v2 rollout at 21:12 UTC.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: router-service@release/2026-03-16-router-v2 — started 2026-03-16T21:10:23Z status: success

alex-ml: quick hypothesis: the new routing middleware introduced a JSON path mapper for legacy targets that flattens nested arrays when a mapping rule mismatches. Possibly a path collision between body.items and meta.items.

jordan-se: Can you repro in staging? if it's a mapping rule, a small repro should show the flattening.

sara-support: I'm spinning up a repro with the exact payload now against the canary instance.

sara-support: repro result — canary/router-v2 returns invoke payload with items=[] and order_id moved to notes. Confirmed locally.

alex-ml: posting quick diff of mapping rules in router-v2 vs router-v1:
```
- mapping: {"from":"body.items.*","to":"body.items"}
+ mapping: {"from":"meta.items","to":"body.items"}
```
looks like the pattern matches greedily and overwrote body.items with meta.items (empty) and the leftover scalar order_id ended up appended to notes field by a downstream serializer.

sysops: Impacted customers? ACME only reported so far, but rolling logs show ~0.8% of action-invokes in prod with missing items since rollout.

sara-support: Proposed mitigations: 1) rollback router-v2 to router-v1 immediately, or 2) apply a hotfix to mapping logic to use strict path anchors and non-greedy match. Which do we want?

alex-ml: rollback is fastest to stop customer impact. Hotfix after rollback + test. I'll open internal issue RI-4021 and assign.

mike-csm: Customer needs ETA for rollback now, they're in a support call. Can we get a rollback within 15m?

deploy-bot: rollback started for router-service@release/2026-03-16-router-v2 -> target: release/router-v1

sara-support: Noted — I'll tell ACME we're rolling back and will follow up with a postmortem and fix plan. :speech_balloon:

jordan-se: after rollback we should run a sanitize check across recent invokes to detect any other route mappings with greedy patterns.

alex-ml: agreed. I'll follow up with unit tests for mapping rules and add explicit non-greedy anchors. Will link PR to issue.

mike-csm: Thanks team. Escalation calmed — customer on the call said rollback fixed new requests. Keeping thread open for postmortem and cleanup.
